subject: Tyska
title: Vocabulary: food and drink
sourceSummary: Words for food, drink, and meals, plus how to order and talk about what you like.

questions.explanation: "Das Abendessen" is dinner/evening meal (literally "evening-eating"). "Das Frühstück" is breakfast, and "das Mittagessen" is lunch.

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Ich ___ Äpfel." (mögen = to like)
questions.opener: Mögen is irregular in the singular forms.
questions.explanation: "Mögen" is conjugated: ich mag, du magst, er/sie/es mag, wir mögen, ihr mögt, sie mögen. "Ich" takes "mag".

questions.prompt: How do you ask a friend "do you like vegetables?"
questions.opener: Swap "ich" for the right form for "du".

questions.prompt: You're at a restaurant. How do you politely order a glass of water?
questions.opener: "Ich hätte gern..." is a polite ordering phrase.
choices: Ich hätte gern ein Glas Wasser, bitte.
questions.explanation: "Ich hätte gern..." (I would like...) is a polite ordering phrase. "Ich will" (I want) sounds more demanding in German than in Swedish.

questions.opener: A common word at all three meals.

questions.prompt: Correct the error: "Meine Schwester magst Reis." (My sister likes rice.)
questions.opener: Check which person the sentence is actually about.
steps: "Magst" is the you-form. The right form for "she" is "mag".
Full sentence: "Meine Schwester mag Reis." (My sister likes rice.)

questions.prompt: Which food, drink, and meal words, and mögen conjugations, should you know at grade 8 level?
questions.opener: Food, meals, and how to express what you like.
questions.answer: Food: das Brot = bread · der Reis = rice · das Fleisch = meat · der Fisch = fish · das Gemüse = vegetables · das Obst = fruit · das Wasser = water · die Milch = milk. Meals: das Frühstück = breakfast · das Mittagessen = lunch · das Abendessen = dinner. Mögen: ich mag, du magst, er/sie/es mag, wir mögen, ihr mögt, sie mögen. Ordering politely: Ich hätte gern... = I would like... · ..., bitte = ..., please.
